intelligence.ai_view: Never certify a surface from its bytes: walk the render at real widths (1919 and 621px here; 1920, 635 and 390 still unmeasured) and fail the page on any single fatal defect — a wrong date is fatal alone. Carry his standing rulings into every rebuild: the logo is the N, top left; the icon bottom right; no glow on either; obsidian black behind so no square shows; the day number stays big in its square AND in Dashboard-style digit tiles, with the date line carrying no second copy; the day's colour governs accents, scrollbars included (Wednesday is Kanye blue); every button to the circle-N standard — flat, plain, high contrast, easy to read.
intelligence.child_view: A calendar's job is to tell you the right day. This one said the wrong day, twice, so it goes back to be fixed — even though lots of its other parts worked great. We always check the real page with our eyes, not just the instructions that built it.
intelligence.essence: Wrong date, purple i, invisible Back — it goes back. The calendar v5 eye walked the page live on 2026-11-18 and sent it back on eight counts, the first of them fatal on its own: the date line says NOVEMBER 26 for both November 18 and November 20, and Wednesday sits flat white instead of lit in its blue. Bytes clean is not a pass — the render is the pass.
intelligence.grandma_view: You know the saying, dear: measure twice, cut once. Well, here we LOOK twice. The page was built correctly on paper, but when a person actually looked at it, the date was wrong and the buttons were hiding. Looking is the real test — paper can't tell you what a page looks like. So back it goes, with a clear list of eight fixes.
intelligence.human_view: Imagine a beautiful wall calendar that insists today is the 26th — on the 18th, and again on the 20th. However lovely the printing, you'd send it back. That's what happened here: the newest calendar page was walked through by eye, on a real screen, and eight things were wrong — a wrong date, colours that ignored the day's own colour, a Back button you can't see, an emblem sitting on top of other buttons. The good bones are real — booking works, the chapters are clear, the picture is real — but a calendar that gets the day wrong has failed at its one job.
intelligence.what_it_means: This note is the correction half of a working pair: the rulings were given live, the build went out, the eye walked it and the verdict came back with evidence. What it proves about the system matters more than the eight defects: the verification loop caught in the render what the bytes could not confess, including counts that disagree with themselves (grid says 2 and 2; month and day lists say 3 and 4) and two test bookings now sitting in the store, quietly owing a cleanup before any count can be trusted.

page.how_it_connects: This correction feeds the interface lane's fix round and stands on the same law as the serving record: a surface is proven only where a person touches it. It connects to the Naya Code and the design canon (colour flows by the day; the circle N is the button standard; obsidian behind every emblem) and to the verification regime that replaced second-seat verdicts — the maker checks, the eye walks, the render decides.
page.machine: Filed: Continuous Distillation, Resolve seat, 2026-11-18 — numbering confirmed by next-sn-number.py (exit 0) immediately before filing. Source: the calendar v5 eye verdict, 2026-11-18 19:17–19:23Z (cloud browser, 1919 + 621px), distilling SN-3336–3372 plus the 19:23–19:33Z lane and eye results. Paired Naya Note: NN-20261118-distilled-calendar-v5-goes-back. HIS RULINGS (18:44–18:50Z, live): the logo is the N, top left; the icon bottom right; no glow on either, obsidian black behind so no square shows. The date and Wednesday must feel ACTIVE, lit up, part of the design. The 18 is the big one: keep the big 18 in its square AND put the 18 in Dashboard-style digit tiles; the date line then just says 'November 26', no second 18. Smart Meet is very flat — bring it alive. Wednesday is Kanye blue, the most beautiful elegant blue; the little 'i' info icon is purple, Sunday's colour — on Wednesday it must be Kanye blue. ALL buttons flat and plain — the circle N is the standard, high quality, high contrast, easy to read, on all pages. KEEP: detail stays in place, no navigation away; dots 3, 4 and 5 are distinct chapters; the 9 dots count, light and jump correctly; Book and Smart Meet work end to end; the King's chamber is a real picture in the month dialog; the top-left N is clean; the 12-second sample is clean. THE EIGHT DEFECTS: (1) the date line is WRONG — 'NOVEMBER 26' for both Nov 18 and Nov 20, no 'November 18th 2026' anywhere, Wednesday flat white not blue; (2) the little 'i' is still purple in the month dialog, not Wednesday blue; (3) 'Back to month' is invisible in the Day menu and the dialog — it works when pressed by name, but a reader cannot see it; (4) the bottom-right emblem sits on a visible black square, covering VIEW, Join and SMART MEET controls and the scrollbar at phone width; (5) the scrollbars are grey, not the day's colour; (6) the day-grid counts disagree — grid says 2 and 2, month and day lists say 3 and 4; (7) the buttons are flat, Smart Meet included, not to the circle N standard; (8) headings, Back and Keep reading, and the dot row are clipped at phone width. Widths not measured: 1920, 635, 390. RE-FILE RECORD (2026-11-19, P-164 recovery): the original page, filed in commit 236062ce97eff9fc0a065d358ff5835002c49f9e, was silently dropped from the main tip by a stale-base tree write; this note is re-filed through the publish-note door with its substance carried from the recovered original page (sha256 cb6596ed958df84cf169fe22cb797ddf350dc4b97adfc9427c12dca468a0939b).
page.the_learning: Bytes clean is not a pass — the render is the pass. A date that says the wrong day fails the page on its own, whatever the bytes say. Owed from this distillation: the fix round for the eight; the eye's two test bookings persist in the store — cleanup owed before the counts can be trusted.
page.what_is_in_it_for_you: For you, Shawn: your rulings from that live session are preserved word for word, the verdict on v5 is on record with its evidence, and the fix round has a checklist it cannot drift from. You never have to re-say the logo, the blue, or the big 18 — they are written here as the standard the next version is judged against.
page.why_it_matters: A calendar is a promise about time; a wrong date breaks the promise at the exact point a citizen trusts it most, and every other defect on the list is the same kind of break in miniature — a control you cannot see, a colour that lies about the day, counts that contradict each other. Sending v5 back with the evidence attached is what keeps the standard real: the next build inherits eight named fixes and the rulings that judge them, instead of a vague feeling that something was off.
